title: Electronics and Communication Engineering Careers (VLSI, communication, core)
summary: Core ECE careers include chip design and verification (VLSI), communication and signal processing, and electronics roles in PSUs and research labs. This path suits students who enjoy circuits, maths and hands-on design, and it also shows how GATE, higher studies and a switch to IT fit in.
outcomes: PSU or Research Lab Engineer (via GATE or own exams)

nodes.title: Circuits, devices and signals
nodes.summary: Networks, electronic devices, analog and digital circuits, and signals and systems are the base for every ECE path. They make up most of the GATE EC syllabus, so strong basics help in core interviews and in GATE.
nodes.proof: Simulate an amplifier and an RC filter in ngspice and explain how your results compare with your hand calculations.

nodes.title: Digital design with Verilog
nodes.summary: Learn to describe circuits in Verilog, write testbenches and read waveforms. This is the entry skill for front-end VLSI roles (RTL design and verification). SystemVerilog and UVM come next for verification jobs.

resources.title: Hardware Modeling using Verilog – NPTEL (IIT Kharagpur)

nodes.proof: Write a UART or FIFO in Verilog with a self-checking testbench that passes in Verilator.

nodes.title: CMOS design and the RTL-to-GDS flow
nodes.summary: Understand CMOS gates, delay, power and timing, then the chip flow: synthesis, floorplanning, placement, routing and static timing analysis. Physical design and STA roles test this, and open tools let you try the full flow for free.

resources.title: VLSI Design Flow: RTL to GDS – NPTEL

nodes.proof: Take a small design through synthesis and place-and-route, and explain its timing report and critical path.

nodes.title: Communication and signal processing
nodes.summary: Cover analog and digital modulation, noise, information theory, basic DSP and electromagnetics. This is the base for telecom, RF and DSP roles. Practise with MATLAB or GNU Radio so you can show working signals, not just formulas.
nodes.proof: Simulate BPSK or QPSK over a noisy channel and plot bit error rate against SNR.

sources.title: NPTEL Communication and Signal Processing domain

nodes.title: Tools employers ask for
nodes.summary: Get comfortable with MATLAB, a SPICE simulator, an HDL simulator, the Linux shell and scripting (Tcl or Python) for running EDA flows. Commercial EDA tools are usually learned in college labs or on the job; free tools teach the same ideas.
nodes.proof: Write a script that runs your simulation or flow from the command line and saves the reports automatically.

nodes.title: One end-to-end core project
nodes.summary: Build one project you can explain in depth, such as a small processor or peripheral in Verilog taken through the open RTL-to-GDS flow, or a software-defined radio receiver in GNU Radio. Depth beats many shallow projects.
nodes.proof: A public repo with RTL, testbench, waveforms and timing/area reports (or a flowgraph and demo video), plus a clear README.

nodes.title: GATE EC, PSUs and government exams
nodes.summary: GATE EC is used for M.Tech admissions and by some PSUs and labs for hiring; each recruiter's advert says whether it uses GATE. ISRO and BEL post their own engineer recruitments, and UPSC ESE has an E&T stream. Use only official pages for dates.

resources.title: GATE 2027 test papers and syllabus – IIT Madras

nodes.proof: Solve two years of past GATE EC papers under timed conditions and keep a log of weak topics.

sources.title: IIT Madras announces GATE 2027 dates and syllabus revision

nodes.title: Higher studies (M.Tech, MS, research)
nodes.summary: An M.Tech in VLSI, communication or signal processing (usually through GATE) leads to deeper design and research roles. Decide early if you want this, because GATE prep overlaps with final-year placements. Check eligibility on the official GATE site.
nodes.proof: A shortlist of 5–8 programmes with their admission route and a written plan for your final year.

nodes.title: Interview preparation and applying
nodes.summary: Core interviews test fundamentals (digital logic, CMOS, analog, communication), your project in depth and aptitude. Revise from past GATE papers, practise explaining your project, and watch official career pages instead of agents who ask for money.

resources.title: GATE 2027 test papers and syllabus – IIT Madras

nodes.proof: A one-page resume with your project, plus a 5-minute walkthrough of it you can give without notes.

nodes.title: Honest check: switching from core to IT
nodes.summary: Many ECE graduates move to software jobs. Your maths and logic help, but you still need one language, data structures, DBMS, OS, networks and real projects. It is a full switch, not a shortcut. Embedded and verification roles sit in between.
